claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy is a single-phase, dendritic BCC alloy.
The TiVNbTa alloy has a low-temperature yield strength of approximately 800 MPa.
The TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of approximately 330 MPa at 1273 K.
The baseline alloy has a compressive strength of approximately 423 MPa at 1273 K.
The proposed intervention is to add approximately 0.3–0.5 wt% Y to TiVNbTa and apply an oxidative high-temperature heat treatment.
Ex situ incorporation of synthesized nano-oxide particles is an alternative to in situ oxidative processing.
Y addition followed by oxidative heat treatment will form Y2O3 nanoparticles in the TiVNbTa matrix.
The resulting Y2O3 particles will be nanometer-scale and uniformly distributed in the BCC matrix.
The Y2O3 nanoparticles will remain thermally stable at elevated temperature.
Y2O3 nanoparticles will pin dislocations in the TiVNbTa matrix.
Y2O3 nanoparticles will stabilize or pin grain boundaries during high-temperature deformation.
Particle pinning will impede grain-boundary sliding at elevated temperature.
Restricting dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding will improve creep resistance.
Oxide dispersion strengthening will mitigate high-temperature softening in TiVNbTa.
The intervention will increase the 1273 K yield strength by approximately 50–100% relative to the 330 MPa baseline.
The treated alloy may attain a yield strength of approximately 500 MPa or more at 1273 K.
The intervention will produce proportional improvements in compressive strength at 1273 K.
The intervention is applicable when oxide dispersions remain stable under high-temperature exposure and thermal cycling.
Applicability requires that the oxide phase neither embrittle the material nor interact adversely with W or CuCrZr.
